findings.description: The Lambda function's environment block embeds a plaintext AWS access key ID and secret access key (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE / wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY). These are stored in Terraform state and visible in the function configuration to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, and they never rotate.

No KMS key is set for the function environment, so the embedded secret values are only protected by the default AWS-managed encryption and can be read in cleartext by any principal permitted to call lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration rather than requiring kms:Decrypt on a customer-managed key.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches, leaving known Node.js vulnerabilities unpatched in the execution environment.

The role grants only sts:AssumeRole via its trust policy and has no attached permissions policy, so the function cannot write CloudWatch logs; failed or malicious invocations will not be auditable. Note the trust policy itself is correctly scoped to lambda.amazonaws.com.
